question.text: A U-tube having a horizontal arm of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, has a uniform cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. It is filled with water of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cc</mi></math>. The volume of a liquid of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cc</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> required to be poured in one arm of the U-tube so that no water is left in the horizontal arm of the tube is (take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
h ρ g = 6 0 × 1 × g

h = 1 5 cm

g=980 cm sec-2
